n: Job responds to Eliphaz, but mostly ignores him. His real concern is finding God.
Even today his complaint is bitter; the hand pressing on him is heavier than his groaning can express.

f.g: The blow or hand that afflicts me.

n: Job’s deepest longing: if only he knew where to find God, he would go right to his throne.

f.w: Oh that I knew where I might find him!

n: Job would lay out his case in order and fill his mouth with arguments, like a man in court.
He wants to hear God’s answer and understand it. Job is not rebelling — he wants to know.
Job trusts that God would not crush him with raw power, but would listen and pay attention to him.

f.w: he would put strength in me
f.g: Better “he would pay attention to me.”

n: There, an upright man could reason with God and be cleared forever by his Judge.

f.w: delivered for ever from my judge

n: But Job can’t find God: he looks forward (east) and back (west), and God isn’t there.

f.g: Also means “east” — ancient people faced east to orient themselves.

n: Left (north) and right (south), he cannot see him. God seems hidden in every direction.
Yet a great statement of trust: even if Job can’t see God, God sees Job’s path, and after the test Job will come out like refined gold.

f.w: I shall come forth as gold

f.g: Tested, as metal is tested by fire.

n: Job has followed close in God’s footsteps and kept his way without turning aside.
He has not drifted from God’s commands, treasuring God’s words more than his daily bread.
But God is unchanging and sovereign; no one can turn him. He does whatever he wills.
God will carry out what he has decreed for Job, and he has many such plans.

f.w: the thing that is appointed for me
f.g: What God has decided for me.

n: So Job feels dread at God’s presence; thinking about it makes him afraid.

f.g: Terrified before him — God feels both longed-for and overwhelming.

n: God has made Job’s heart faint; the Almighty has filled him with fear.

f.g: Makes me faint-hearted, weak with fear.

n: Job is not silenced by the darkness, though deep gloom covers his face. He keeps speaking despite it all.

f.w: I was not cut off before the darkness
f.g: The Hebrew is difficult; it may mean “I am not silenced by the darkness.”
